chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man shake hands with a woman who is not his mahram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except from behind the garment.'

key_terms.ذِي مَحْرَمٍ: mahram (close relative with whom marriage is prohibited)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on men shaking hands with non-mahram women?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of shaking hands with non-mahram women by specifying the condition of doing so 'from behind the garment' (*min wara’ al-thawb*). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between a light, cloth-mediated touch—which is generally considered permissible—and direct skin-to-skin contact, which is often deemed impermissible to avoid *fitnah* (temptation). The phrase highlights the emphasis on modesty and the preservation of social boundaries within Islamic etiquette.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can the man shake the hand of the woman who is not with a sanctity (with him)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except from behind the cloth’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from abu Basir who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if one can shake hands with women who are lawful for marriage. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not permissible except from behind the cloth.’”
